# secopsctl search

Search the SIEM (read-only): udm events, raw logs, stats, saved searches

## search event

Inspect one event by id: enriched UDM (default), --udm, or --raw log

```text
secopsctl search event <id> [flags]
```

```text
Fetch one event's detail by id (the base64 udm.metadata.id from a search
result). Default prints the ENRICHED UDM event (geo / threat-intel / entity
overlays). --udm prints the unenriched UDM event; --raw prints the original
raw log line(s). --token treats the argument as a search token instead of an id
(for --udm).
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--raw` | bool | false | print the original raw log line(s) for the event |
| `--token` | bool | false | treat the argument as a search token instead of an event id (with --udm) |
| `--udm` | bool | false | print the unenriched UDM event(s) |

**Examples**

```bash
secopsctl search event 'AAAA…=' --json
  secopsctl search event 'AAAA…=' --raw
```

## search export

Export ALL matching events to CSV (server-side; not capped at --limit)

```text
secopsctl search export <filter> [flags]
```

```text
Export every event matching a UDM query over [start, end) to CSV, projected
onto the chosen columns. Unlike `query udm` (capped at --limit, client-side),
this is the server-side bulk export and returns the complete result set.

--fields are the console column labels (e.g. timestamp, user, hostname,
"process name", "raw log", or any udm.additional.* path); unsupported labels
are reported and skipped. --out writes to a file instead of stdout.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--case-sensitive` | bool | false | case-sensitive matching (default: case-insensitive, like the console) |
| `--fields` | string | - | comma-separated column labels (default: timestamp,user,hostname,"process name") |
| `--from` | string | - | explicit start time (RFC3339 / ISO-8601); overrides --hours |
| `--hours` | int | 24 | look-back window in hours when --from is not given |
| `--out` | string | - | write the CSV to a file instead of stdout |
| `--to` | string | - | explicit end time (RFC3339 / ISO-8601); default: now |

**Examples**

```bash
secopsctl search export 'metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_DNS"' --hours 24 --out dns.csv
  secopsctl search export 'principal.hostname = "host-01"' --fields timestamp,user,hostname
```

## search generate-query

Generate a UDM query from natural language (Gemini); do not run it

```text
secopsctl search generate-query <natural language>
```

```text
Translate a plain-English question into a UDM query via Gemini and print it,
along with any time window the model inferred. Use `gemini search` to also run it.
```

**Examples**

```bash
secopsctl gemini generate-query 'failed logins to admin accounts in the last hour'
```

## search raw

Content-based raw-log search: print FULL raw lines matching a regex

```text
secopsctl search raw <pattern> [flags]
```

```text
Search raw (ingested) logs by CONTENT (searchRawLogs): <pattern> is a regex
matched against the raw bytes — use a distinctive substring of the log type you
want (it matches ANY log containing the pattern). Prints each match's FULL raw
log line, one per line, for `parsers run --logs -`:

  secopsctl search raw 'GET /healthz' --limit 50 | \
    secopsctl parsers run KONG_GATEWAY --cbn parser.conf --logs -

Unlike `query udm --raw` (scopes by metadata.log_type; needs a UDM event), this
reaches even logs with no parser at all. --unparsed adds `parsed = false`.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--from` | string | - | explicit start time (RFC3339 / ISO-8601); overrides --hours |
| `--hours` | int | 24 | look-back window in hours when --from is not given |
| `--limit` | int | 100 | max raw lines to fetch |
| `--to` | string | - | explicit end time (RFC3339 / ISO-8601); default: now |
| `--unparsed` | bool | false | restrict to truly-unparsed logs (parsed = false) |

## search run

Run a UDM query loaded from a file or stdin (`-`)

```text
secopsctl search run (--file <path> | --file -) [flags]
```

```text
Run a UDM event search whose predicate is read from a file (--file <path>)
or stdin (--file -), so a tracked .udm file is a runnable, reviewable query.
Blank and #-comment lines in the file are ignored. Same window/--limit/--raw
semantics as `query udm`.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--all` | bool | false | return the complete result set via the search-view engine (reports the total match count) |
| `--fields` | string | - | comma-separated UDM field paths to project (e.g. metadata.event_type,principal.hostname) |
| `--file` | string | - | path to a UDM query file, or - to read from stdin |
| `--format` | string | - | output format: table\|json\|jsonl\|csv (default: table on a terminal, jsonl when piped) |
| `--from` | string | - | explicit start time (RFC3339 / ISO-8601); overrides --hours |
| `--hours` | int | 24 | look-back window in hours when --from is not given |
| `--limit` | int | 10000 | maximum number of events to return |
| `--out` | string | - | write results to a file instead of stdout |
| `--raw` | bool | false | print each matched event's FULL raw log line instead of the event summary |
| `--to` | string | - | explicit end time (RFC3339 / ISO-8601); default: now |

**Examples**

```bash
secopsctl search run --file detections/failed-logins.udm --hours 24
  echo 'metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_CONNECTION"' | secopsctl search run --file -
```

## search saved

Server-side saved & shared searches (Search Manager)

```text
secopsctl search saved
```

```text
List, run, and manage server-side saved searches (the console's Search
Manager). Saved searches live on the tenant and can be shared across the org
(--share). Running `saved` with no subcommand lists them.
```

## search stats

Run a stats/aggregation UDM query (match:/outcome:) and print the result table

```text
secopsctl search stats <aggregation-query> [flags]
```

```text
Run an AGGREGATION UDM query — one carrying a `match:`/`outcome:` projection,
the exact YARA-L a dashboard chart uses. `query udm` runs an event search and
rejects an aggregation with a 400; this executes it over the same
`dashboardQueries:execute` path dashboard charts use and prints the computed
columns and rows (`--json` for the raw result), so a chart query can be
validated end to end from the CLI before `dashboards add-chart`.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--clear-cache` | bool | false | bypass the query cache (read from the database) |
| `--from` | string | - | explicit start time (RFC3339 / ISO-8601); overrides --hours |
| `--hours` | int | 24 | look-back window in hours when --from is not given |
| `--limit` | int | 0 | max rows to print (0 = all) |
| `--to` | string | - | explicit end time (RFC3339 / ISO-8601); default: now |

**Examples**

```bash
secopsctl search stats --hours 24 'metadata.log_type != ""
  match: metadata.log_type
  outcome: $c = count(metadata.id)
  order: $c desc'
```

## search udm

Run a UDM event search over a time window

```text
secopsctl search udm <filter> [flags]
```

```text
Run a UDM event search over [start, end]. The window defaults to the last
--hours; --from/--to (RFC3339 / ISO-8601) override it.

--raw prints each matched event's FULL raw (ingested) log line instead of the
event summary — one per line, to pipe into a parser test. This is how to pull
the raw logs for a log type whose parser is missing/broken (they normalize to
GENERIC_EVENT):

  secopsctl search udm 'metadata.log_type = "KONG_GATEWAY" AND \
      metadata.event_type = "GENERIC_EVENT"' --raw --limit 50 | \
    secopsctl parsers run KONG_GATEWAY --cbn parser.conf --logs -

With --raw, --limit defaults to 100 (one raw fetch per matched event).
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--all` | bool | false | return the complete result set via the search-view engine (reports the total match count) |
| `--fields` | string | - | comma-separated UDM field paths to project (e.g. metadata.event_type,principal.hostname) |
| `--format` | string | - | output format: table\|json\|jsonl\|csv (default: table on a terminal, jsonl when piped) |
| `--from` | string | - | explicit start time (RFC3339 / ISO-8601); overrides --hours |
| `--hours` | int | 24 | look-back window in hours when --from is not given |
| `--limit` | int | 10000 | maximum number of events to return |
| `--out` | string | - | write results to a file instead of stdout |
| `--raw` | bool | false | print each matched event's FULL raw log line instead of the event summary |
| `--to` | string | - | explicit end time (RFC3339 / ISO-8601); default: now |

**Examples**

```bash
# network connections in the last 6 hours
  secopsctl search udm 'metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_CONNECTION"' --hours 6

  # a fixed window, machine-readable
  secopsctl search udm 'principal.hostname = "host-01"' \
      --from 2024-01-02T00:00:00Z --to 2024-01-03T00:00:00Z --json
```

## search validate

Validate a UDM query's syntax without running it

```text
secopsctl search validate <query>
```

```text
Check a UDM query for syntax errors without running a search. Prints the
detected query type and (when invalid) the error message; exits non-zero on an
invalid query so a script/agent can gate on it.
```

**Examples**

```bash
secopsctl search validate 'metadata.event_type = "NETWORK_DNS"'
```
